title: Incident report: a size limit that rejected valid drawings
summary: Báo cáo giải thích vì sao bản vẽ hợp lệ bị từ chối sau một thay đổi cấu hình, cách nhóm khôi phục dịch vụ và cải thiện việc kiểm tra giới hạn tải lên.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: On Tuesday morning, the support team received several messages from customers who could not attach drawings to maintenance requests. The customers could still create requests, write descriptions, and add photographs. However, a drawing produced a message saying that the file was too large. Most affected customers were preparing work for the following week, so they needed a reliable way to share the drawings before technicians reviewed their requests. Support opened an incident at 9:20 after confirming that the problem affected more than one customer organisation.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: The first investigation focused on the files themselves. A support colleague obtained permission to use one customer's drawing and tried it in a separate test request. The drawing opened normally on her computer and was smaller than the maximum size stated on the upload screen. The rejected drawing was twelve megabytes, while the screen advertised a twenty-megabyte limit. Two other examples showed the same pattern. This made a damaged file less likely, although the team continued checking different file types rather than assuming that every failed attachment had the same cause.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: An engineer compared the current service settings with the settings recorded before Monday's deployment. The application still allowed twenty-megabyte attachments, but another component that received incoming requests had a lower limit. The receiving component had been configured to accept only ten megabytes. That setting came from a standard configuration used by a smaller internal service. The deployment had included several unrelated improvements, and the person reviewing it had checked the application changes without noticing that the attachment limit in the shared configuration had also changed.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: The incident lead considered two temporary responses. One option was to tell customers to reduce their drawings or send them through a separate channel. That would allow some work to continue, but it would also create extra steps and make attachments harder to find later. The team chose to restore the previous receiving limit. An engineer prepared the configuration change while support drafted a short update. They did not increase the advertised maximum, because this incident concerned an unintended reduction rather than a request to accept larger drawings.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: Before applying the correction, the engineer tested files below, near, and above the advertised maximum in the test environment. The checks included a photograph, a drawing, and a document containing several pages. A second engineer reviewed both the setting and the test results. The corrected configuration reached the live service at 10:35. Support then repeated the upload using the original example and confirmed that the drawing appeared on the intended request. Monitoring continued for the rest of the morning because a successful single upload would not prove that every affected customer could work normally.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: Support contacted the customers who had reported the problem and explained what had changed. Customers needed to upload rejected drawings again. Their written request details remained available, so they did not need to start each request from the beginning. The team avoided saying that all work had been recovered automatically. Some customers had already shared drawings through other channels, and support asked them to attach those drawings to the original requests when convenient. This would give technicians one place to review the description and the supporting material before arranging a visit.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: The review found that the existing deployment check used only a small photograph. It confirmed that uploading worked, but it did not check whether the published limit was still accurate. Future deployment checks will include a file near the advertised maximum. The team also added the receiving limit to the configuration review checklist. These changes were preferred to a general instruction to be more careful, because reviewers needed a specific item they could inspect. The technical lead assigned an owner to each action and asked for evidence of completion before the next configuration release.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: The incident was closed after the afternoon review found no further failures caused by the reduced limit. A separate request to accept much larger drawings remained on the product team's list, but it was not included in the correction. The team agreed that this separation made the result easier to explain: the service once again matched the promise already shown to customers. The final report recorded the start and end times, the affected action, and the configuration difference. It also acknowledged that the customer reports helped reveal a gap in the team's own checks.

title: Workplace procedure: arranging a week at another office
summary: Quy trình hướng dẫn nhân viên xin làm việc tạm thời tại văn phòng khác, cân nhắc mục đích chuyến đi, chỗ ngồi, thiết bị và trách nhiệm với nhóm hiện tại.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: Employees sometimes ask to spend a working week at another company office. A visit can help colleagues solve a shared problem, understand a local process, or build a relationship with a team they usually meet online. However, the receiving office must have enough space and someone available to help the visitor. This procedure covers visits of up to five working days. Longer arrangements need a separate discussion because they can affect staffing plans and the visitor's regular responsibilities. A visit should have a clear purpose beyond simply changing the place where someone opens their laptop.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: The employee begins by discussing the idea with their manager. Together, they identify the work that would benefit from being done in person and decide whether a shorter visit would be enough. The request must include two specific outcomes. For example, an analyst might aim to observe the local ordering process and agree a common report format with the receiving team. General statements such as meeting people are not sufficient on their own. The manager also checks whether the employee has deadlines that would be difficult to meet while travelling or attending local sessions.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: After that discussion, the employee contacts the receiving office coordinator with proposed dates and the agreed purpose. Requests should arrive at least ten working days before the visit. The coordinator checks desk availability, planned events, and whether the relevant colleagues will actually be present. An apparently quiet week may still be unsuitable if the people the visitor needs are attending training elsewhere. The coordinator can suggest different dates rather than rejecting the idea completely. The employee should wait for this check before making travel arrangements or promising a fixed schedule to other colleagues.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: The receiving team names a local host once suitable dates have been found. The host does not need to spend the whole week beside the visitor, but they provide a contact point and help arrange the first morning. The local host prepares a simple arrival schedule. This includes the entrance to use, the time to arrive, and the first planned conversation. If the host will be away on one day, they name another colleague for practical questions. A clear handover avoids leaving the visitor to ask several busy people the same basic questions.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: Desk arrangements should be confirmed before the visit. Some desks have a monitor but no keyboard, while others are reserved for staff who use particular equipment. Visitors bring their own laptop. The coordinator tells them which additional items are available and whether any equipment needs to be booked. A visitor who needs a quiet place for regular customer calls should mention this early. The office may offer a call room for certain periods, but a desk booking does not automatically include a private room for the entire week.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: The visitor remains responsible for work already agreed with their home team. Before leaving, they share a brief availability note explaining when they will be in local sessions and when they can respond to routine questions. The visit does not transfer the employee's normal deadlines to the local host. If a deadline and a local activity conflict, the employee and their manager decide which takes priority. They should make that decision openly, rather than allowing colleagues in either office to assume that someone else has taken responsibility.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: Plans can change after approval. If the receiving team loses desk space or an essential colleague becomes unavailable, the coordinator contacts the visitor as soon as the problem is known. A visit may be shortened, moved, or replaced with an online session if its purpose can still be achieved that way. The employee should also report changes from their side, including new deadlines. Keeping the original dates is not useful if the planned work can no longer happen. Any changes to booked travel follow the company's existing travel process.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: Within three working days of returning, the employee sends a short note to their manager and the local host. The note compares the visit's results with the two outcomes in the original request. It should record agreements, unfinished questions, and the person responsible for each next step. The purpose is to turn the visit into useful shared work rather than a long account of every conversation. If the employee recommends another visit, they explain what remains to be done and why another in-person session would help more than an ordinary online meeting.

title: Outdoor pool notice: collecting a season pass before opening weekend
summary: Thông báo hướng dẫn người dân nhận thẻ mùa tại hồ bơi ngoài trời, kiểm tra ảnh và tên, chọn cách nhận phù hợp và xử lý trường hợp thẻ chưa sẵn sàng.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: The Riverside Outdoor Pool opens for the summer on Saturday, 8 June. People who have bought a season pass can collect their cards before opening weekend, when the entrance is expected to be busy. Advance collection is optional, but it should reduce the time spent waiting on the first morning. The collection desk will operate in the community centre rather than at the pool. This allows staff to prepare the pool entrance while another team deals with pass photographs, names, and collection questions in a quieter indoor space.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: The advance desk opens from Tuesday to Friday, between ten in the morning and six in the evening. On Thursday, it stays open until eight for people who cannot come during ordinary working hours. No collection appointment is required. However, the desk has only two staff members, so visitors may need to wait if several households arrive together. Please bring the booking reference from your purchase confirmation. Staff use this reference to find the correct order, especially when several people have similar names or a household has bought more than one type of pass.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: A season pass includes a photograph because each card is for one named person. If you uploaded an acceptable photograph when buying the pass, the card should already be prepared. People without an uploaded photograph can have one taken at the collection desk. The photograph service adds time to the visit, particularly for households collecting several cards. Staff will check that the face is clear and that the image matches the person named on the pass. Decorative filters and photographs showing several people cannot be used for the card.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: Please check the printed name before leaving the desk. Small spelling mistakes are easier to correct while the order is still open on the staff member's screen. Staff can correct a spelling error at the collection desk. A request to replace one named person with another is different and must be reviewed by the membership team. The collection staff cannot approve that change immediately. If your confirmation already contains the wrong name, contact the membership team before visiting so they can explain what information they need.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: One adult may collect several prepared cards from the same household order. This can save a second journey, but it works only when the photographs have already been accepted and no personal details need checking. Bring the order reference and check every card before leaving. Cards requiring a new photograph must be collected by the named person. For this reason, a parent collecting their own finished card may still need to return with a child whose photograph is missing. Staff will explain which cards are ready and which remain incomplete.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: People who cannot use the advance desk can collect their passes at the pool after it opens. On opening weekend, card collection and entry will use separate queues. A person collecting a card should join the collection queue first, then move to the entrance queue after receiving it. Buying a pass in advance does not reserve a place in a swimming session. Session availability is shown through the pool's usual booking system. Please check your planned session separately rather than assuming that a completed card guarantees entry at any particular time.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: Some cards may not be ready because a photograph was rejected or information is still being checked. If you have an incomplete order, staff can write down the next action and the team responsible for it. The note is a collection update, not an entrance pass. If your card cannot be completed before a booked session, speak to the pool reception team with your order reference and session confirmation. They will check the situation and explain the available arrangement. Please do not join the ordinary entrance queue expecting the gate staff to prepare a card.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: During the advance collection period, the community centre's rear car park will be closed for line painting. Visitors can use the front pedestrian entrance, and bicycles can be left at the stands beside the main doors. A short stay at the desk may take longer if photographs or corrections are needed, so allow enough time for your journey home. After opening weekend, routine card questions return to the pool reception desk. The community centre will no longer hold uncollected cards once the temporary collection desk has finished operating.

title: Migration proposal: replacing a free-text business-hours field
summary: Đề xuất chuyển giờ làm việc của chi nhánh từ văn bản tự do sang các khoảng giờ có cấu trúc, giữ thông tin cũ để đối chiếu và yêu cầu con người kiểm tra các trường hợp mơ hồ.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: The branch directory currently stores business hours in a single text field. Staff have used that field in several ways: some write a weekly schedule, some describe exceptions, and others add instructions about calling before a visit. This flexibility helped the directory grow quickly, but it now makes the information difficult to reuse. The customer portal can display the text, yet it cannot reliably answer a simple question such as whether a branch is open on Wednesday afternoon. This proposal introduces structured weekly hours while retaining useful information that does not belong in a timetable.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: The proposed weekly schedule contains separate opening periods for each day. A day may contain two periods when a branch closes during lunch. An empty day means that no regular opening period has been recorded for that day; during migration, it must not automatically be interpreted as a confirmed closure. Each imported schedule will have a review status. This distinction matters because an unclear old entry and a deliberately closed day may look similar on a screen, although they represent different levels of confidence in the underlying information.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: The migration will begin with a copy of the existing branch records. Entries following a clear pattern, such as Monday to Friday with the same opening and closing times, can be prepared for review automatically. The conversion tool will not guess the meaning of unclear abbreviations. Records containing phrases such as afternoons vary will go directly to the review list. The old text will remain visible beside the proposed schedule. This gives the branch reviewer enough context to confirm a straightforward conversion or correct an interpretation before customers see it.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: Notes about access and appointments will move into a separate visitor-information field. For example, a branch may have regular opening hours but require visitors to call before bringing large equipment. That instruction should remain available without being treated as part of the weekly timetable. Reviewers must decide whether a sentence describes opening times, visitor instructions, or both. The proposal does not remove a note simply because it cannot be converted into hours. Preserving these details takes additional review time, but losing them could make a technically tidy directory less useful to actual visitors.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: Branch coordinators will review their own records during a two-week checking period. Each coordinator receives a list showing the original entry, the proposed hours, and any unresolved question. A second reviewer checks records with split opening periods or uncertain notes. Ordinary records need only the local coordinator's confirmation. This approach avoids asking two people to inspect every simple entry while still giving more attention to cases where interpretation matters. Coordinators who are away must name a substitute, because an unanswered review request cannot be treated as agreement.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: Publication will happen in two stages. First, staff will see the structured schedule inside the directory while customers continue to see the existing text. During this stage, the team can compare real records and correct presentation problems without changing the public information. Only confirmed schedules will appear in the customer portal. Unconfirmed branches will continue displaying their old text with a message asking visitors to check directly with the branch. This temporary mixture is less consistent visually, but it avoids presenting an uncertain schedule as a reliable answer.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: Holiday arrangements will be handled separately from the regular week. A coordinator can record an exception for a particular date without changing the normal Monday or Tuesday schedule. Holiday exceptions will take priority over the regular weekly schedule. The first release will support a closed day or a replacement set of opening periods. More complicated arrangements will remain in visitor information until the team understands how often they occur. This limit keeps the initial work manageable and gives coordinators a clear explanation of what the new system can represent.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: The migration will be considered complete when every active branch has either a confirmed schedule or an explicitly recorded unresolved case with an owner. Completion will therefore mean that uncertainty is visible and assigned, rather than hidden behind an empty field. The original entries will be kept in the internal migration record for later comparison. After four weeks, the team will review customer questions and coordinator feedback. It will use those results to decide whether further schedule features are necessary, instead of adding options simply because the old text field allowed unlimited wording.

title: Review procedure: checking a meeting transcript before circulation
summary: Quy trình kiểm tra bản chép lời cuộc họp trước khi chia sẻ, phân biệt sửa lỗi ghi nhận với thay đổi phát biểu, xác nhận số liệu và giữ vai trò riêng của danh sách hành động.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: The operations team records some planning meetings so that colleagues who cannot attend can review the discussion later. A recording can be useful, but many people prefer a written transcript because they can search it and read only the relevant section. The transcript is a record of the discussion, not a list of approved decisions. Before it is circulated, it needs a limited review to catch errors that could change what readers understand. This procedure explains who performs that review and how corrections are made without rewriting the meeting after it has happened.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: At the start of an eligible meeting, the chair explains that a recording and transcript will be created for the named internal audience. Anyone raising a concern should speak to the chair before the recording begins. The chair also identifies sections that should be kept outside the shared transcript, such as a discussion containing confidential supplier figures. The review process does not give permission to distribute the recording more widely. If the intended audience changes, the chair must consider that separately instead of assuming that an accurate transcript is suitable for everyone.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: After the meeting, the organiser prepares a draft and labels it clearly as awaiting review. The draft includes the meeting date, the participant list, and time markers for important sections. Time markers help reviewers return to the recording when a sentence looks doubtful. The first review focuses on names, quantities, dates, and statements that appear to reverse the speaker's meaning. It does not aim to make every sentence sound formal. Natural hesitation and repeated words may remain when they do not prevent a reader from understanding the discussion.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: Each participant receives the sections in which they made substantial contributions. Participants have two working days to report accuracy concerns. A useful correction identifies the time marker, the disputed wording, and what the recording actually supports. Participants should not replace a clear statement merely because they now prefer a different position. If their view has changed since the meeting, they can provide a separate dated note. Keeping that distinction protects readers from mistaking a later opinion for something that everyone heard and discussed at the original meeting.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: Numbers require particular care because a small error can affect later planning. If the draft says fifteen units but the recording is unclear, the organiser asks the speaker to check the relevant source rather than choosing the number that seems more likely. Uncertain figures are marked for confirmation. When the source is a planning sheet, the final transcript can point to that sheet instead of presenting an uncertain spoken number as settled fact. The organiser records who confirmed the figure, so another colleague can ask a useful follow-up question if needed.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: The chair reviews passages that describe agreements or future work. Sometimes a participant suggests an action, but the group never decides to take it. The transcript should preserve that difference. A separate action list records only tasks that the chair confirms were agreed. Each task needs an owner and an expected completion date. The action list links back to the relevant discussion where helpful, but readers should not have to search several pages to discover what they are expected to do. This also allows an action to be updated without altering the historical transcript.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: Once the review period ends, the organiser applies supported corrections and sends the chair a short list of unresolved points. The chair may delay circulation of a doubtful section while allowing the rest of the transcript to proceed. The final document includes a review date and a contact for reporting later errors. Changes made after circulation are recorded in a correction note. A silent replacement would make it difficult for colleagues to know whether their earlier reading was still accurate, particularly if they had already used a figure or quotation in another internal document.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: The team will try this procedure for six meetings before deciding whether to keep it. Reviewers will report how much time they spent and which types of error caused the most difficulty. The organiser will also ask absent colleagues whether the transcript helped them understand the discussion. A perfect transcript is not the only goal; the process must be useful enough to justify the work it creates. If people mainly need decisions and responsibilities, the team may place greater emphasis on the action list while retaining transcripts only for discussions where the surrounding reasoning matters.

title: Service estimate: restoring binoculars for weekend birdwatching
summary: Bản báo giá trình bày các vấn đề quan sát được ở ống nhòm, phạm vi bảo dưỡng, lựa chọn thay dây đeo và cách khách hàng quyết định giữa sửa chữa với mua thiết bị mới.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: Thank you for bringing your binoculars to the workshop on Monday. You explained that you use them for short birdwatching walks and that they have become difficult to adjust. You also mentioned a cloudy area that is especially noticeable when looking towards a bright sky. This estimate covers the condition we observed during the initial inspection and the work we can offer. It is intended to help you decide whether a limited service meets your needs. We have not included changes that would turn the binoculars into a different model or improve their original specifications.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: The outside of the binoculars shows normal wear around the hand grips. The carrying case still closes properly, although its lining is loose in one corner. The main concern is the focus wheel, which moves unevenly during adjustment. The focus wheel becomes stiff near the middle of its movement. We also found marks on the accessible outer lens surfaces. During our indoor viewing check, the image did not appear doubled. That observation is useful, but it does not establish the condition of every internal part or guarantee the result of a complete service.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: We recommend beginning with cleaning the accessible surfaces and servicing the focus mechanism. The proposed basic service costs forty-eight pounds. This includes the initial work and a viewing check afterwards. We will then compare the cloudy area with the condition recorded at inspection. If it remains, we may need to discuss further examination rather than assuming that more external cleaning will solve it. Opening additional parts is outside this basic estimate. We will contact you before undertaking work that increases the price or changes the agreed scope.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: The neck strap is worn where it passes through one of the attachment points. You can keep using the existing carrying case, but we suggest replacing the strap if you plan to carry the binoculars outside the case during walks. A replacement strap costs twelve pounds. It is optional and is not included in the forty-eight-pound basic service. We have one plain black version available. If you prefer a wider strap from another supplier, we can leave this item out and show you the attachment points when you collect the binoculars.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: There are two reasonable ways to proceed. You can approve the basic service first and make a second decision if the cloudy area remains. Alternatively, you can decline the work and compare replacement binoculars before spending more on these. The first option may preserve an item you already find comfortable to hold, but it leaves some uncertainty about the final image. The second avoids further repair spending, although a replacement would need to be tried carefully. Our estimate does not assume that a new pair will automatically suit you better.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: If you approve the basic service by Thursday afternoon, we expect to finish it during the following week. The work takes place in a scheduled workshop slot, so an early reply helps us keep that slot available. The estimate remains valid for thirty days. After that period, we will confirm the price and availability again before accepting the work. If further examination is recommended, we will give you a separate estimate and a new expected completion date. Please tell us if you have a planned trip, but do not assume that an additional service can fit the original collection date.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: At collection, we will ask you to adjust the focus and look at several objects from the workshop window. You should bring your usual glasses if you normally wear them while using the binoculars. This check gives you an opportunity to assess comfort as well as the image. It is more useful than collecting the case without trying the equipment. We will explain which work was completed and whether any observed issue remains. If the result does not match the agreed work, please raise the concern before leaving so we can examine it together.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: To approve the estimate, reply with the service reference and state whether you want the basic service alone or the basic service with the replacement strap. We will acknowledge your choice before starting. No replacement strap will be fitted without approval. If you decline, we can arrange collection of the binoculars in their inspected condition. We will keep the inspection notes with the estimate so you can refer to them later. This should help you compare the practical benefit of the proposed work with the cost of another pair, without feeling obliged to decide immediately.

title: Release plan: recording why a maintenance ticket is closed
summary: Kế hoạch phát hành bổ sung lý do đóng phiếu bảo trì để phân biệt công việc hoàn thành, yêu cầu trùng và yêu cầu không còn cần thiết, đồng thời tránh tự suy diễn dữ liệu cũ.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: The maintenance application currently gives a ticket one final status: closed. That status covers several different situations. A technician may have completed the work, a coordinator may have discovered a duplicate request, or a customer may no longer need the visit. Managers can find some explanations in comments, but those comments are inconsistent and difficult to compare across many tickets. The next release will ask for a closure reason. The purpose is to make the final outcome clearer without turning the closing step into a long form that people avoid completing.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: The first release offers four reasons: work completed, duplicate request, no longer required, and unable to proceed. The last option covers cases where the team cannot continue, such as a customer who has not supplied necessary information after the agreed follow-up process. It should not be used simply because the technician is busy today. Choosing unable to proceed requires an explanatory note. The other reasons allow a note but do not require one, unless another existing rule already applies to that type of maintenance request.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: The closing screen will show the reason choices beside a short description of each one. A technician who selects duplicate request must identify the ticket that will continue to hold the work. This link helps a colleague understand where to look next instead of treating both requests as finished jobs. If the continuing ticket cannot be found, the user can return to the request and resolve that question before closing it. The team rejected a design that accepted any typed ticket number, because an unchecked number could point to nothing useful.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: Reports will distinguish closure from completion. The completed-work total will include only tickets closed with the work completed reason. Tickets marked duplicate or no longer required will appear in separate totals. This may make the completed-work figure lower than the old closed-ticket figure, even when the team has done the same amount of practical work. Managers will receive a comparison note before release so they understand the change. The application will not present the new total as directly equivalent to the old measure without explaining the different definition.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: Existing closed tickets will not be assigned guessed reasons from their comments. Older tickets will retain a reason of not recorded. A coordinator may add a reason later if there is clear supporting information, but the application will record that update as a later change. This approach leaves a gap in historical reporting, yet it avoids creating confident-looking data from uncertain text. The product team considered automatic classification and decided that it would need a separate evaluation before it could be used for records that managers rely on.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: The release will begin with one maintenance team for a week. During the trial, observers will check whether people understand the choices and whether the additional step interrupts routine work. Trial feedback will focus on the reason selected, the time needed to close a ticket, and questions raised by users. The team will also review a small sample of closed tickets with supervisors. If a reason is regularly misunderstood, its description will be revised before wider release. Adding more categories immediately is not the preferred response to every unusual case.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: Customers will continue to receive a short closing message, but the message must reflect the selected reason. A duplicate request will direct the customer to the continuing ticket rather than claiming that maintenance has been completed. For an unable to proceed outcome, the coordinator will review the message before it is sent. Internal notes will not be copied automatically into customer messages. This matters because an internal explanation may contain shorthand or discussion that is useful to colleagues but confusing to the person who originally requested the work.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: After the trial, the release owner will compare user feedback with the reporting benefits. Wider release will proceed only when the closing process is clear enough for ordinary use and the report labels explain the new measure. If the feature must be withdrawn, tickets already closed with a reason will keep that information. The old closing screen can return without deleting the data gathered during the trial. The team will then decide whether the difficulty came from the screen, the categories, or the organisation's own understanding of what a closed maintenance ticket means.

title: Handover brief: maintaining the company history timeline
summary: Tài liệu bàn giao hướng dẫn duy trì dòng thời gian lịch sử công ty, kiểm tra nguồn, xử lý ngày tháng chưa chắc chắn và quyết định nội dung phù hợp trước khi công bố.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: This brief is for the colleague taking over the company history timeline during my three-month assignment with the events team. The timeline appears in the visitor area and in a digital version used by new employees. It contains selected milestones rather than a complete account of everything the company has done. Requests for additions arrive throughout the year, especially when teams finish a large project or discover an old photograph. Your main responsibility is to keep the entries accurate, understandable, and balanced while making sure that requests do not disappear into an unattended inbox.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: New requests arrive through the history inbox and should be added to the request register before any research begins. The register records the proposed event, the person making the request, the suggested date, and the material provided. Acknowledge each request within three working days. The acknowledgement confirms receipt, not acceptance onto the timeline. Some contributors assume that sending a photograph guarantees publication, so make this distinction clear. If essential information is missing, ask a focused question instead of sending a long general request for more detail.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: For each proposed entry, look for evidence that supports both the event and its date. An announcement, a dated project record, or a contemporary newsletter may be useful. A photograph can support what happened without establishing when it happened. Several older photographs have dates written on their backs, but those dates were sometimes added years later. Keep the contributor's explanation alongside the material and record any uncertainty. The aim is not to dismiss people's memories; it is to avoid presenting a precise date more confidently than the available evidence allows.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: If two sources give different dates, first check whether they describe different stages of the same event. A product may have been demonstrated in March, made available to selected customers in April, and launched more widely in June. Conflicting dates may refer to different milestones rather than an error. Ask the relevant team what claim the proposed entry is meant to make. If the exact day cannot be established but the year is clear, the timeline can use the year alone. Do not invent a day merely to match the format of neighbouring entries.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: The communications manager reviews proposed additions once a month. Before that meeting, prepare a short description explaining why each event matters beyond the team that submitted it. The monthly review considers significance, clarity, and available space. It also checks whether recent entries have crowded out earlier developments or work from less visible departments. A request can be accurate and still be unsuitable for the public timeline. In that case, suggest another home for the material, such as the internal project archive, rather than telling the contributor that the event has no value.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: Images need a separate check before publication. Confirm where the image came from and whether the company has permission to use it for the proposed display. Some photographs supplied by former employees were taken by an outside photographer, so possession of a copy does not settle the publication question. Unclear image permissions must be referred to the communications manager. This handover does not ask you to resolve specialist questions yourself. If a useful image cannot be cleared in time, the entry may proceed without it rather than holding up every approved change.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: After approval, update the digital timeline first and check the wording in its actual display. A sentence that looks short in the register may wrap awkwardly on the visitor screen. Printed panels are updated in quarterly batches. Until the next batch is ready, keep a list of differences between the digital and printed versions so reception staff can answer questions. Every published entry should have an internal record linking it to the approved wording and supporting material. This makes later corrections possible without relying on whoever remembers the original discussion.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: At the end of each month, send the communications manager a brief status note covering published entries, requests awaiting evidence, and decisions still needed. Do not measure progress only by the number of additions. Resolving an uncertain date or giving a contributor a clear explanation can be useful work even when the timeline does not change. Before my return, prepare a handback note with open cases and their next steps. Include any repeated difficulties you noticed, because they may show that the request form or review process needs improvement rather than more individual reminders.

title: Community notice: booking the shared fruit press for harvest weekend
summary: Thông báo giải thích cách đặt máy ép trái cây dùng chung, chuẩn bị dụng cụ và trái cây, chia sẻ thời gian công bằng và xử lý khi thành phẩm ít hơn dự kiến.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: The neighbourhood garden group will run a fruit-pressing weekend on 21 and 22 September. Residents can bring apples or pears from their gardens and use the group's press with help from a volunteer. The event is intended for household quantities, not commercial production. Booking is required because the equipment can serve only one group at a time. The press will be set up under the covered area beside the community shed, which provides space for preparation and keeps the main garden path clear for other visitors.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: Each household can reserve one forty-five-minute slot. This includes an introduction, fruit preparation at the station, pressing, and clearing the area for the next group. Please estimate the amount of fruit when you book. The volunteers use that information to judge whether it is realistic for the available time. If you have a larger quantity, they may suggest sharing it across a later community session rather than promising that everything can be processed in one slot. Booking a second consecutive slot is not available during the first round of reservations.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Bring fruit that you have already sorted and checked at home. The station is not set up for dealing with large amounts of unwanted fruit or garden waste. Volunteers will inspect the fruit again before using the equipment and may set unsuitable pieces aside. Mixed varieties can be pressed together. You do not need to separate every variety into a different box, although keeping a note of your mixture may help if you want to repeat it next year. Please remove leaves, loose twigs, and other material before packing the fruit for the journey.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: The group provides the press, preparation trays, and the tools used at the station. You must bring containers for collecting your juice. Choose containers that are clean and can stand securely while being filled. The volunteers cannot promise how much juice a particular box of fruit will produce, so bring some spare capacity rather than relying on a precise estimate. A few empty containers will be available for unexpected shortages, but these are a backup supply. They should not be treated as a guaranteed part of the booking.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: A volunteer will explain the process at the beginning of your slot and remain at the station while the press is used. Only the assigned volunteer operates the press. Residents can help with the preparation tasks that the volunteer identifies. Children are welcome to watch from the marked waiting area with an accompanying adult. The purpose of this arrangement is to keep the working area organised, especially when several family members arrive together. Please do not bring extra helpers without mentioning them in your booking, because space beside the station is limited.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: The event charge is six pounds per household slot. The charge covers use of the station and the materials needed to clean it between groups. Payment is taken when the booking is confirmed. If you cancel at least two days before the event, the group will offer your place to someone on the waiting list and return the payment. Later cancellations will be considered individually. If the group cancels your session because the equipment is unavailable, you can choose a refund or a place at a replacement session.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: Please arrive ten minutes before your booked time and report to the welcome table. There is no need to unload everything immediately; a volunteer will tell you when the station is ready. A late arrival will not extend the finishing time of the slot. If a delay means that only part of your fruit can be processed, you can take the remainder home or ask whether space becomes available later. The volunteers cannot remove another household's booking to complete a late group's work, even when the reason for the delay is understandable.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: After pressing, you will leave with your filled containers and any fruit that was not processed. The group will collect the remaining pressed material in its designated garden-waste containers. Before leaving, check that you have all your own boxes and lids, since similar containers can easily be confused. The welcome table will also collect comments about the booking system and the length of the slots. If demand is high, the group may organise another day later in the season. That decision will depend on volunteer availability as well as the number of residents interested.

title: Support investigation: a reference search that ignored leading zeroes
summary: Cuộc điều tra hỗ trợ tìm ra việc ô tìm kiếm chuyển mã tham chiếu thành số và bỏ số không đầu, gây nhầm kết quả dù dữ liệu gốc vẫn đúng. Nhóm chọn sửa cách tìm và bổ sung kiểm tra có ý nghĩa.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: A warehouse coordinator contacted support because searching for a delivery reference returned a different record from the one printed on her paperwork. She had entered 00418, but the first result showed reference 418. Both records belonged to the same organisation, and both described deliveries made during the previous month. The similar details made the result look plausible at first. The coordinator noticed the problem only when she compared the destination with the printed document. She asked whether someone had changed the reference or whether the search itself was treating the two values as equivalent.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: Support began by checking the two records directly. Their references were different in the record view, and the dates of their most recent edits did not suggest a recent change. The stored reference still contained its leading zeroes. The coordinator then opened the intended record from the delivery list and confirmed that its paperwork attachment matched her document. This narrowed the investigation: the record could be found through the list, but entering its reference in the search box did not reliably put it ahead of a different record.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: An engineer reproduced the problem in a test organisation containing several deliberately similar references. The search form handled letters and numbers differently. References containing a letter were passed through as text, while references made entirely of digits were converted before the search request was sent. The search form converted an all-digit entry into a number. In this application, that conversion removed the leading zeroes from 00418. The service therefore received 418 rather than the exact reference the coordinator had typed. The stored records themselves had not been rewritten by this search.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: The behaviour came from an older search form designed for the application's internal record numbers. When customer delivery references were added later, the same form was reused to reduce development work. The examples used during that change all contained a letter or started with a non-zero digit. Tests did not include references beginning with zero. The review concluded that the feature had been checked against examples that were too narrow. It did not find evidence that the warehouse coordinator had entered the reference incorrectly or that another user had edited away its zeroes.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: Support needed a temporary method that the coordinator could use while the correction was prepared. She could open the record from the delivery list, but the list was long and this was slower than her usual search. Support recommended narrowing the delivery list by date and destination. Those two filters made it easier to identify the intended record without relying on the affected reference search. The support note explained that this was a workaround, not a change to how references should be written. Staff should continue entering the full reference shown on the source document.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: The proposed correction keeps delivery references as text from entry through to the search request. It also distinguishes searching a customer reference from searching an internal record number. An exact reference match will appear before partial matches. This ordering matters because the coordinator may still see several related results, but the one matching her complete entry should be easiest to identify. The team decided against removing partial matching entirely, since some users search with only the middle part of a reference when the full document is not available.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: Before release, the team checked references with leading zeroes, letters, spaces, and several different lengths. It also checked two records whose references differed only by their leading zeroes. The tests examined the request sent to the service as well as the displayed results. Checking only the visible search box would have missed the conversion, because the coordinator's original entry had remained visible there. Support repeated the customer's example after the correction reached the test environment and confirmed that 00418 appeared as the first exact match.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: The correction was released on Friday afternoon after review by a second engineer. Support asked the coordinator to repeat her normal task and confirm that the result was now useful in practice. No stored references needed changing. The closing message explained the cause, the correction, and the removal of the temporary workaround. The team also added a reminder to its feature checklist: examples should include the forms of data customers actually use, not just the forms most convenient for developers. This was a small search change, but it affected confidence in finding the right delivery.
